meta.title: Trace: Fixes thread safety issue in Trace class causing high CPU usage
meta.body_summary: Added thread safety to Trace class dictionary operations using locks, then switched to ConcurrentDictionary per review feedback, to fix high CPU usage from cross-region hedging due to concurrent non-thread-safe Dictionary access.

perf_labels.notes: Copilot fixed thread safety with locks, then refactored to ConcurrentDictionary per review; maintainer requested perf validation but PR closed without merge.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 10338 changed lines, this is a large-scale change by absolute volume, but the overwhelming majority comes from master merges; the actual trace fix is ~100 lines. The PR was closed without merge after maintainer requested perf run validation, which was not provided.

review_details.concern_detail: FabianMeiswinkel requested switching from locks to ConcurrentDictionary with lazy initialization to avoid locking overhead; later kirankumarkolli requested a performance run validation, which was not completed before the PR was closed.
review_details.performance_claim: Fixing thread safety of dictionary operations reduces high CPU usage from cross-region hedging.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Agent initially used locks, but maintainer guided towards ConcurrentDictionary; needed multiple iterations to correctly implement Lazy<ConcurrentDictionary> and preserve API contract; lacked performance validation, leading to closure.

detection_detail.code_reading: FabianMeiswinkel identified that locks were unnecessary and suggested ConcurrentDictionary; also noted lazy initialization needed and missing thread-safety comments on interface, providing detailed review.
detection_detail.ci_auto: Pipeline failures due to ConcurrentDictionary element ordering were detected and raised by sourabh1007.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: A multi-threaded unit test was added to verify thread safety, but no before/after performance data or repro steps for high CPU was provided.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: PR was closed without merge after maintainer requested perf run validation; no fix-in-PR occurred.

core_change_summary.description: In Trace.cs, switched from non-thread-safe Dictionary access to ConcurrentDictionary with lazy initialization (Lazy<ConcurrentDictionary>) for thread-safe add/update operations; updated ITrace interface to remove misplaced thread-safety comments; added a multi-threaded test in TraceTests.cs.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Most churn comes from master merges (API contracts, benchmarks, etc.) unrelated to the trace fix; the trace fix itself is ~100 lines.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: added locks to dictionary operations in Trace class.
Added unit test for thread safety.
Updated ITrace documentation with thread-safety comment.
Per FabianMeiswinkel review: replaced locks with ConcurrentDictionary.
Moved thread-safety comments from ITrace to Trace per review.
Reverted to Lazy<Dictionary> with locks after maintainer noted overhead concern; then switched to Lazy<ConcurrentDictionary>.
Fixed AddDatum to throw ArgumentException on duplicate key to match original Dictionary.Add behavior.
Improved thread safety test assertions, then reverted to simpler assertions per review.
Added OrderedConcurrentDictionary to preserve element order, then reverted due to pipeline ordering issues; final revert to ConcurrentDictionary.
Multiple master merges introducing unrelated changes.

review_signals.summary: Suggested using ConcurrentDictionary instead of locks in Trace class.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot replaced locks with ConcurrentDictionary in commit 67a1c40.

review_signals.summary: Insisted that the data field should be Lazy<ConcurrentDictionary<string, object>> to minimize memory overhead.
review_signals.action_taken: After reverting to locks momentarily, Copilot implemented Lazy<ConcurrentDictionary> in commit 66efc2a.

review_signals.summary: Noted that TryAdd silently ignores duplicate keys; required throwing ArgumentException to preserve original Dictionary.Add behavior.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot added conditional throw in commit bdc9edbc.

review_signals.summary: Pointed out that thread-safety comment on ITrace interface is wrong; should be moved to Trace implementation.
Questioned validity of test assertion (Data.Count > 0) as sufficient proof of thread safety.
review_signals.action_taken: Test was improved and then reverted to simpler form after discussion.

review_signals.summary: Reported pipeline failures because ConcurrentDictionary changes order of 'Client Configuration' and 'DistributedTraceId'.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot added OrderedConcurrentDictionary, then reverted to plain ConcurrentDictionary after maintainer request.

review_signals.summary: Explained that ConcurrentDictionary is always the right call and minimal overhead; approved the final approach.
Requested a performance run validation before merging.
review_signals.action_taken: No perf run was provided; PR was eventually closed.

review_signals.summary: Triggered Azure Pipelines via /azp run multiple times.

collaboration_trajectory: Copilot opened PR with lock-based thread safety fix and unit test.
FabianMeiswinkel immediately suggested ConcurrentDictionary and detailed design corrections.
Copilot iterated through several implementations: lock, ConcurrentDictionary, Lazy<Dictionary>, Lazy<ConcurrentDictionary>.
Discussion on test assertions and API contract preservation led to further commits.
CI failures due to element ordering surfaced; Copilot attempted OrderedConcurrentDictionary, then reverted.
Maintainers eventually approved the design, but kirankumarkolli blocked merge pending performance validation.
PR was closed without merge, likely due to lack of performance evidence.
